newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Up to 100,000 protesters march in Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: Up to 100,000 protesters march in Belgrade.

text.p: Up to 100,000 protesters marched in Belgrade on Sunday and Serbia's opposition leaders vowed to demonstrate until President Slobodan Milosevic backed down in a crisis over alleged election fraud.

"Our protests will last until Serbia becomes a legal state," Zoran Djindjic, a prominent opposition leader, said on the 28th consecutive day of protest against the annulling last month of local election results.

Students were joined by trade union members in the march which grew as it snaked around Belgrade for a rally in the central square. "Many are still joining the column of marchers," one opposition leader said.
There was a carnival atmosphere with music being played along some sections of the route.
Members of the crowd waved American, German and Italian flags as well as opposition flags. Belgraders switched the lights of their flats on and off as the march passed, in gestures of support.
The rally will take place at about 1630 GMT.
